notes: The reference case: 3 a.m., almost everyone home and asleep, alarm audible in every flat, fire starting on floor 12.
The same night with a corridor-only alarm, which is the condition Proulx measured at 515 s rather than 169 s. The comparison against night_fire12 isolates audibility.
A weekday afternoon: a quarter of residents are out, nobody is asleep, and the people at home skew older and less mobile.

One floor of the same tower, for checking the model by hand. Four flats and about seven residents - small enough to read every number and trace every one of them to a source. Note that at this size the published distributions are NOT reproduced: seven draws cannot recover a fitted curve, and the figures that depend on a population are reported but should not be read as conforming. Build the whole tower when you want the distributions to mean something, and this when you want to audit them.
